papers.title: Octavius: A High-Performance Analysis Toolkit for Galaxy Simulations
papers.abstract: Increased computing power and more efficient codes have allowed cosmological simulations of galaxy formation to grow massively in scale: the analysis of their outputs has consequently become a big data computational challenge. We present Octavius, a high-performance, hybrid-parallel simulation analysis toolkit. Octavius ingests a simulation snapshot with associated halo catalogue, locates galaxies with a 6D friends-of-friends algorithm, then produces an HDF5 catalogue of properties for haloes, subhaloes, and galaxies. The analysis is fast and memory efficient: we compare the performance against the widely used predecessor toolkit, Caesar, and show Octavius delivers order-of-magnitude improvements in speed with a factor of >5 reduction in peak memory. We demonstrate near-linear strong scaling of compute and linear peak memory scaling with the number of halo-assigned particles. Compute times scale with the superlinear computational load of larger haloes; we note the pipeline is presently I/O-limited. The code is written in Python and uses a declarative, plugin-based architecture so as to be easily extensible. Octavius can currently analyse SIMBA, SWIFT-KIARA, SWIFT-EAGLE, SWIFT-COLIBRE, and TNG snapshots; AHF, HBT-HERONS, and SUBFIND halo catalogues are supported. Properties computed include masses, galaxy photometry with dust attenuation, and kinematic, radial, morphological, and virial quantities. Output catalogues are easily accessed through a provided user API. The code is open sourced at this https URL

papers.title: A Smoothly Truncated Dark Matter Spike around a Black Hole in an Einstein-Cluster Model
papers.abstract: We introduce a finite dark matter spike around a static, spherically symmetric black hole, with a general power-law index and an Einstein-cluster stress tensor. Smooth inner depletion and outer truncation ensure that the density and its first radial derivative vanish at both boundaries, while a single normalization preserves the prescribed exterior mass. The resulting spacetime contains an inner vacuum gap, a matter region with vanishing radial pressure, and an outer Schwarzschild vacuum. We derive the enclosed mass, density maximum, local logarithmic slope, and matched metric without surface layers, including exact polynomial-root representations of the matter-region metric for spike indices $7/3$ and $3/2$. Energy conditions and radial stability of the constituent circular orbits constrain the admissible configurations. A sufficient bound guarantees these properties for an inner edge at or beyond the Schwarzschild marginal-stability radius and also ensures positivity of the massless-scalar potential. Comparisons at a common mass budget examine how boundary regularity and radial concentration jointly affect the gravitational response. Shadows and light deflection also depend on the global redshift and mass calibration. Scalar waves matched across the three regions with one infinity-normalized time coordinate distinguish local gap-redshift effects from propagation through the complete geometry. The smoothly truncated profile provides a controlled equilibrium model for investigating how finite support and mass redistribution affect black hole observables; its taper scales, formation, and collective stability require additional physical input.

papers.title: G92.4+5.0: A Perseus Arm superbubble associated with the H II region CTB 102
papers.abstract: Superbubbles are vast hot cavities carved out by the stellar winds and supernovae of clusters of high-mass stars. We investigate G92.4+5.0 (the CTB 102 superbubble), a Perseus Arm superbubble associated with the HII region CTB 102. We use new and archival radio observations (total intensity, rotation measure, and HI spectral line) from the Dominion Radio Astrophysical Observatory Synthesis Telescope, combined with single-antenna data from the Effelsberg Medium Latitude Survey, the Global Magneto-Ionic Medium Survey, and the HI4PI survey to provide data on large structures. The upper region of the superbubble is faint in HI. In order to detect its full extent, we supplement our observations with H-alpha data from the Wisconsin H-Alpha Mapper Survey and the Ziegenbalg Survey, and observe H-alpha emission in the upper region. We measure the CTB 102 superbubble to be at least ~170 pc wide and ~420 pc tall, with an expansion rate of ~12 km/s in the lower regions of the superbubble and ~22.5 km/s in the upper regions. The elongated structure and increasing expansion rate with height are consistent with the evolutionary properties of a superbubble described by the Kompaneets model. We fit the Kompaneets model to the CTB 102 superbubble and obtain an estimated age of 1-6 Myr. This supports a possible scenario in which the stellar cluster currently ionizing CTB 102 is the expansion energy source for the superbubble. Alternatively, if the superbubble expanded under the power of a previous generation of stars, the current CTB 102 stellar cluster may have formed in the walls of the superbubble.

papers.title: Parity-violating scalar-tensor theory revisited: complete basis up to $d=4$ and Hamiltonian analysis
papers.abstract: We construct complete bases of parity-violating generally covariant scalar-tensor (GST) and spatially covariant gravity (SCG) monomials up to derivative grade $d=4$. Including all derivative partitions, each description contains one $d=3$ and thirteen $d=4$ linearly independent monomials. At the level of Lagrangians, we find six integration-by-parts relations that reduce polynomial-type Lagrangians to combinations of one $d=3$ and seven $d=4$ monomials with general coefficient functions. We derive the correspondence between the two bases, retaining general coefficients and total derivatives, and establish their independence under integrations by parts. Among the seven $d=4$ SCG monomials, five contain neither the lapse velocity nor the time derivative of the extrinsic curvature. For the two remaining monomials, we perform a Hamiltonian constraint analysis with a standard Einstein-Hilbert kinetic term and a lapse-dependent potential. On the regular branches considered, the lapse-velocity term propagates four degrees of freedom (DOFs), while the extrinsic-curvature-velocity term propagates six DOFs, whether present alone or together with the lapse-velocity term. papers.title: The box within the Universe: anisotropies in periodic cosmological simulations I. Dark-matter-only simulations
papers.abstract: The vast majority of cosmological simulations employ periodic boundary conditions to achieve statistical homogeneity and to mimic the infinite spatial extent of our Universe. In a cubic periodic domain the Green function breaks full rotational invariance and introduces a geometry-induced anisotropy in the gravitational interaction. We quantify how this intrinsic anisotropy affects cosmic structure growth and investigate the extent to which it biases the commonly used large-scale structure and halo-based observables in dark-matter-only simulations. We analyse an ensemble of 498 cosmological dark-matter-only $N$-body simulations in cubic $T^3$ topological manifolds, evolved to $z=0$, spanning box sizes from $L=6.25\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ to $L=100\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ at fixed mass and force resolution. We compare anisotropy-sensitive statistics across the suite, including the matter power spectrum, halo abundance, merger histories, shapes and alignments, and filament orientations. Finite periodic boundaries imprint orientation-dependent signatures aligned with the box geometry. These signatures propagate beyond the largest modes and can induce systematic shifts in both field-level and halo-level statistics. The detectable effects propagate to scales much smaller than the box size. Our results demonstrate that periodic-box anisotropy is a non-negligible source of systematics for small simulation volumes, including those commonly employed in modern hydrodynamical simulations.

papers.title: Instabilities of Simpson-Visser black bounces sourced by a phantom scalar and nonlinear electrodynamics
papers.abstract: We study the linear stability of Simpson-Visser ``black-bounce'' space-times (regular black holes and wormholes) under spherically symmetric (monopole) perturbations, taking as a source a phantom scalar field with a self-interaction potential and a magnetic field within nonlinear electrodynamics (NED). The metric contains two parameters: the mass $M$ and the bounce parameter $a >0$, such that $a \leq 2M$ corresponds to black holes and $a > 2M$ to wormholes. The stability problem reduces to a boundary-value problem for a Schrödinger-like equation with a certain effective potential. All space-times under study are found to be unstable, and the corresponding exponential growth rates are calculated. For black holes the results are obtained without complications, while the wormhole stability problem faces difficulties that seem to be previously unnoticed. Thus, the Darboux transformation, used to remove the wall shaped $\approx 2/z^2$ in the effective potentials at wormhole throats ($z$ is the tortoise coordinate), creates nonphysical poles outside the throat for $a/(2M) \lesssim 4.98$. We circumvent this difficulty by using a gauge-invariant approach in the spirit of Cremona, Pizzocchero and Sarbach, leading to a master equation with a simple and regular potential. Its further analysis reveals unstable modes: the mode with a variable throat radius is always present; for $a/(2M) \gtrsim 4.98$ there are two real growing throat modes, which merge into a complex-conjugate pair (oscillatory instability) for smaller $a$. A further analysis reveals three exceptional points that separate ranges of $a/(2M)$ with different perturbation regimes. Furthermore, the leading unstable black-hole and wormhole modes approach the same limiting growth rate $M\kappa\simeq 0.10121$ as $a/(2M)$ approaches unity from either side.

papers.abstract: We investigate how spatial resolution affects emission-line diagnostics in the interstellar medium (ISM) of the Small and Large Magellanic Clouds (SMC and LMC) using SDSS Local Volume Mapper (LVM) data obtained at and degraded to 19, 42, 170 pc (for the SMC) and 17, 68, 272 pc (for the LMC), respectively. Diffuse ionized gas is particularly sensitive to this mixing, while H{\alpha} selected ionized regions exhibit more robust behavior across resolutions. With false assignment limited to $10^{-3}$ at the other mass, the power to identify either mass is at most 1.584\%. papers.title: Torsion talks only to spin: the CMB temperature as a test of energy exchange in Einstein-Cartan cosmology
papers.abstract: The cosmic microwave background temperature at $z=0.886$ is known to $2\%$ from molecular absorption towards PKS~1830$-$211; CO absorbers and Sunyaev-Zel'dovich clusters extend the measurement to $z\simeq3$. We use them on a question that cosmologies with torsion leave open. When the geometry exchanges energy with several matter components, which of them receives it? In Einstein-Cartan theory the Noether identities of each sector fix the answer. A sector's energy-momentum fails to be conserved only in proportion to its own spin, so minimally coupled light, which has none, is conserved whatever the torsion does. A metric-affine cosmology fitted to DESI DR2 distributes the exchange ``universally'' among all fluids, radiation included; the photons then gain almost a third of their energy. If the photons stay a blackbody, as FIRAS requires of any source set by local conditions, the model predicts a background colder than $T_{0}(1+z)$ by $7\%$ at $z\simeq0.9$ and by $8.5\%$ at $z\gtrsim3$, with no free parameter. PKS~1830$-$211 gives $5.08\pm0.10\,\mathrm{K}$ against a predicted $4.78\,\mathrm{K}$; with the CO absorbers it favours the standard scaling by $\Delta\chi^{2}=13$, and 18 Planck cluster bins give $\chi^{2}=50.8$ versus $15.5$. Under the same reading the primary anisotropies would change their spectral shape by amounts Planck excludes. If dark matter carries the spin instead, $H(z)$ moves by less than $10^{-4}$ below $z=3$ at the fitted parameters and $T(z)$ is standard again.

papers.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
papers.abstract: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs. For individual DMs, the correlation with the bandpowers is at the per cent level. Neglecting the cross-covariance changes the width of the $\chi^2$ distribution by only 0.8 per cent, so the two observables can be treated as effectively independent for wide-area surveys. In a joint forecast with an LSST-like weak lensing survey, adding the Macquart relation tightens constraints on the physical baryon density by 32 per cent and on the mean host contribution by a factor of 4.1, while improving baryonification parameters by only about 5 per cent, indirectly through the host contribution. Finally, we show that the redshift distribution of FRBs without identified hosts, which enters every DM power spectrum, can be reconstructed by inverting their DMs with the jointly fitted mean relation without biasing the inferred parameters, whereas a 20 per cent error in the mean relation biases the DM power spectrum by up to 2$\sigma$ per band for $5\times 10^5$ FRBs.

papers.title: Unveiling the Origins of Local Group Galaxies with ELT-SHARP: An Overview of Science Cases
papers.abstract: The $\Lambda$CDM paradigm successfully describes large-scale cosmic structure, yet tensions possibly persist on galactic and sub-galactic scales. The Milky Way and the Local Universe offer a uniquely accessible laboratory to probe these discrepancies through chemo-dynamical studies of resolved stellar populations. Understanding disk assembly, dynamical heating, and galactoseismology requires wide-field coverage and high-angular-resolution near-infrared spectroscopy capable of penetrating dust-obscured regions and resolving crowded stellar environments. We propose science cases exploiting \textsc{SHARP}, a multi-mode near-infrared spectrograph for Extremely Large Telescopes and future space facilities. Operating over $0.95$--$2.45\,\mu$m in a single exposure, \textsc{SHARP} enables efficient access to key stellar and gas tracers across the Galactic bulge, disk, halo, and nearby galaxies. The \textsc{NEXUS} mode provides adaptive-optics-assisted multi-object spectroscopy over a $1.2'\times1.2'$ field with spectral resolutions up to $R\sim17{,}000$, enabling gas and stellar kinematics. Complementarily, the \textsc{VESPER} multi-IFU mode delivers spatially resolved spectroscopy in crowded regions, allowing reconstruction of internal kinematics and stellar population gradients on sub-arcsecond scales. Combined with surveys such as \textit{Gaia}, APOGEE, LAMOST, LSST, 4MOST, and ELT--MOSAIC, this project will map six-dimensional phase-space structures of disk and bulge stars, stellar streams, and nearby disk galaxies (e.g. LMC, SMC). The data will enable investigations of bars, spiral arms, warps, flares, and satellite interactions, providing critical constraints on disk evolution, merger history, and dark matter substructure, and providing stringent tests of $\Lambda$CDM on the smallest accessible scales.

papers.title: Asymptotic safety is not generic
papers.abstract: Asymptotically safe quantum gravity proposes a non-perturbative ultraviolet completion of gravity in which the high-energy behavior is controlled by an ultraviolet fixed point---the Reuter fixed point---for which there is robust evidence from a wide range of settings and truncations. The existence of asymptotic safety requires non-trivial zeros of beta functions, raising the question of how generic such fixed-point solutions are. In this work, we tackle this issue by investigating chiral perturbation theories. We focus on SU(2) and SU(3) chiral models, which share key features with gravity such as perturbative non-renormalizability or nonlinear interactions, but which are known to admit a different ultraviolet completion via new degrees of freedom. Using the functional renormalization group, we study these theories within a quartic-derivative truncation and find no evidence for an interacting fixed point. This result suggests that asymptotic safety is not generic, but rather a feature pertaining to certain special systems.

papers.abstract: The Central Molecular Zone, a dense and gas-rich region surrounding the Galactic Center, hosts numerous dense molecular gas cores that provide unique environments to probe dark matter interactions. Our results highlight the potential of dense molecular cores near the Galactic Center as promising targets for constraining dark matter interactions with future observations.

papers.title: On Entanglement Dynamics in Holographic Theories
papers.abstract: Entanglement entropy (EE) is central to modern theoretical physics, yet its calculation in interacting theories with nontrivial time dependence remains challenging. In this thesis, we investigate the real-time dynamics of EE in strongly coupled quantum field theories (QFTs) using the Anti-de Sitter/Conformal Field Theory (AdS/CFT) correspondence. We first examine EE evolution in an exactly solvable two-dimensional conformal field theory (CFT) with an inhomogeneous sine-square deformation (SSD). We argue that the unconventional time evolution driven by the SSD Hamiltonian can be viewed as a change in spacetime foliation, producing new horizons in the dual three-dimensional bulk. Holographic EE calculations agree with CFT results in all comparable cases. We then study entanglement dynamics in generic chaotic quantum many-body systems. In the limit of late time and large regions, these dynamics are believed to admit an effective entanglement membrane description. In 2d CFTs, a degenerate membrane tension reproduces several entropy dynamics results, unlike the non-degenerate tension in higher dimensions. Using holography, we show that capturing reflected entropy in 2d CFT requires an additional degree of freedom in the membrane description. We further show that a conventional non-degenerate tension emerges when the CFT undergoes a relevant deformation, holographically dual to a planar Banados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ) black hole with scalar hair and an interior Kasner universe. We then develop a membrane effective theory for reflected entropy dynamics in higher dimensions. Finally, we apply the membrane theories for reflected entropy to study the time evolution of multipartite entanglement signals. We found that scrambling dynamics generate multipartite entanglement with rich structures.

papers.abstract: We study how boundary correlation functions encode the charge dependence of the renormalised Euclidean action of an AdS$_3$ black brane. The scalar two-point function and the shift symmetry of its source determine the matter Weyl anomaly, which fixes the logarithmic temperature dependence of the quadratic term in the charge expansion. At quartic order, the connected four-point function comes from tree-level graviton exchange. Integrating it against the linear source, with an infrared cutoff on the overall scale of the integral, reproduces the quartic coefficient of the action per unit length. At each higher order, the corresponding Catalan coefficient predicts the integrated sum of all connected tree-level Witten diagrams.

papers.title: Finite is not enough: Triviality bounds in nonlocal field theories
papers.abstract: An ultraviolet-finite theory need not be ultraviolet complete. We obtain a bound on the infrared coupling by requiring perturbative control at all scales. This bound varies only at the percent level across the examples we consider. We expect similar bounds in models of discrete spacetime. Thus, requiring ultraviolet completeness improves the predictivity of nonlocal theories.

papers.title: Why a Multi-Cycle Treasury Program is Essential to Maximize JWST's Scientific Contributions to Galaxy Formation
papers.abstract: The Genesis Initiative is an extragalactic community-wide effort to coordinate white papers in response to the STScI Multi-Cycle Treasury (MCT) concept call. Two of JWST's primary science goals are to discover and characterize the first stars and galaxies, and to understand how they evolved into the galaxies we see today - questions whose fundamental importance has been affirmed by the past three decadal surveys. JWST's first five years have surpassed expectations, revealing a bounty of unexpected discoveries about the early universe. Yet these discoveries have raised as many questions as they have answered, and key mission goals remain unmet. Transforming this excitement into a quantitative physical understanding of early galaxy formation requires a uniform, statistically controlled legacy dataset that the current portfolio of smaller, heterogeneous programs cannot provide. The history of the Hubble Space Telescope offers a clear precedent. Its most transformative extragalactic results came from large, coordinated surveys far exceeding what the standard time-allocation process typically approves, and these uniform datasets remain scientifically productive decades later. We argue that JWST is now poised for the same leap. Answering the field's central open questions demands coordinated, community-led surveys of ~1000-2000 hr, with uniform and well-characterized selection functions that are structurally impossible within single-cycle programs. Such an investment is time-critical while JWST's instruments remain at peak performance, and would maximize synergy with ALMA, Euclid, Roman, Rubin, and future facilities. We therefore urge STScI to open a MCT channel, enabling the bold, ambitious surveys needed to understand how galaxies evolve from first light to the present day.

papers.title: On the importance of medium-resolution continuum spectroscopy for JWST's extragalactic legacy
papers.abstract: We argue for a significant investment of JWST time into an extremely deep medium-resolution NIRSpec MSA survey targeting a large, representative sample of high-redshift $(z>1.5)$ galaxies, specifically intended to obtain high-SNR continuum detections. This is only possible with JWST, and no planned future instrumentation has similar capabilities, meaning that obtaining such observations with JWST must be urgently prioritised. The vast majority of existing archival NIRSpec observations are not deep enough for continuum science, being focused on the detection of emission lines. Deeper continuum data opens up the ability to constrain a much wider range of key galaxy physical parameters, including stellar population ages and metallicities, stellar kinematics and neutral gas physical properties, inflows and outflows. Such measurements will provide crucial insight into quenching physics, galaxy dynamical masses, merger histories, pristine early star-formation, reionization and the physics of Little Red Dots, as well as enabling all of the emission-line science that can be achieved with shallower observations. To facilitate future survey planning, we present an empirically derived relationship between rest-optical continuum SNR in JWST NIRSpec medium-resolution data, rest-optical apparent magnitude and exposure time, which we show to be independent of redshift (and hence the grating used). We then provide a 1000-hour sketch survey plan based on achieving the continuum SNR $=20$/pixel necessary to constrain key physical properties and scaling relations for a large galaxy sample at $z>1.5$. We finally discuss NIRSpec sky subtraction strategies, which are of critical importance for continuum SNR.

papers.title: Eddies that ride the flow: a model of turbulence with Richardson dispersion and anomalous dissipation

papers.title: Improving Gravitationally Induced Entanglement in Interferometric Configurations
papers.abstract: Proposals to detect gravitationally induced entanglement between massive particles offer a promising pathway toward probing the quantum nature of gravity. We perform a systematic geometric optimization and comparative analysis of Stern--Gerlach (SG) and Mach--Zehnder (MZ) matter-wave interferometers for this purpose, deriving exact analytical expressions for the gravitational phase of each configuration. Our first key result is that geometric optimization is indispensable. For commonly assumed experimental parameters, neglecting the optimization of geometric ratios can suppress the accumulated phase, and hence the detectability of entanglement, by up to several orders of magnitude. Second, we provide a complete comparative analysis of two SG orientations (linear and parallel) and three MZ orientations (translation-symmetric, mirror-symmetric, and parallel-arms). papers.title: Can Two-Point Correlations Determine Gravitational Waves from Sound Waves?

papers.title: A slow spin to win: The gradual kinematic evolution across metallicities of the proto-Galaxy to the high-$α$ disc
papers.abstract: Observational studies are identifying stars thought to be remnants from the earliest stages of the hierarchical mass assembly of the Milky Way, referred to as the proto-Galaxy. We use red giant stars with kinematics and [$\alpha$/M] and [M/H] estimates from Gaia DR3 data to investigate the relationship between azimuthal velocity and metallicity, aiming to understand the transition from a chaotic proto-Galaxy to a well-ordered, rotating (old) disc-like population. This model is designed to capture the conditional distribution P(v$_\phi$ $\mid$ [M/H]) with a 2-component Gaussian Mixture Model with fixed azimuthal velocities means and standard deviations. To quantify the spin-up of the high-$\alpha$ disc population, we extend this two-component model by allowing the mean velocity and velocity dispersion to vary between the spline knots across the metallicity range used. We also compare our findings with existing literature using traditional Gaussian Mixture Modelling in bins of [M/H] and investigate using orbital circularity instead of azimuthal velocity. Our findings show that the metal-poor high-$\alpha$ disc gradually spins up across [M/H] $\sim$ -1.7 to -1.0, while the low-$\alpha$ sample exhibits a sharp transition at [M/H] $\sim$ -1.0. This latter result is due to the accreted debris dominating the metal-poor end, underscoring the critical role of [$\alpha$/M] selection in studying the (old) disc evolution of the Milky Way. These results indicate that the proto-Galaxy underwent a slow, monotonic spin-up phase rather than a rapid, dramatic spin-up at [M/H] $\sim$ -1.0, as previously inferred.

papers.title: Are magnetic fields in cosmic voids primordial?
papers.abstract: The existence and origin of magnetic fields in cosmic voids remains an open question: Observational evidence inferred from gamma-ray spectra of TeV blazars has been debated for over a decade, while early-Universe magnetogenesis models typically invoke physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. In the conducting intergalactic medium, these fields spread through turbulent magnetic diffusion, and the galaxies residing within voids reduce the required propagation distance to a few Mpc, a scale bracketed by current estimates of the turbulent diffusivity. In the regime where the propagation distance is sufficient, the superposition of randomly oriented galactic dipoles produces volume-filling void fields with a white-noise spectrum and amplitudes well above the lower bounds inferred from the absence of GeV halos around TeV blazars. These fields constitute an astrophysical background that must be accounted for before void fields are interpreted as relics of primordial magnetogenesis, and they could account for the void fields without requiring primordial fields at all. papers.abstract: Combinations of the most recent CMB, BAO, and SNeIa datasets, when analyzed using the CPL parametrization, $w(a) = w_0 + (1 - a) w_a$, exclude $\Lambda$CDM at $\gtrsim\!3\sigma$ in favor of a dark energy equation of state (EoS) parameter that crosses the phantom divide. We confirm this behavior and show that it persists when DESI BAO data are replaced by SH0ES $H_0$ measurements, despite the known tension between these probes in the presence of CMB data. In both cases, the constraints favor a transition from an early-time phantom-like phase to a late-time quintessence-like phase, with the crossing occurring at different redshifts depending on the dataset combination. The probability that a phantom divide line (PDL) crossing does not occur within the expansion history is excluded at significance levels ranging \mbox{between $3.1\sigma$\,--\,$5.2\sigma$.} To investigate whether the apparent PDL crossing is a genuine feature preferred by the data or an artifact of the linear form of the CPL parametrization, we isolate the PDL crossing feature by introducing two modified versions of CPL that explicitly forbid it: CPL${}_{>a_\mathrm{c}}$ and CPL${}_{<a_\mathrm{c}}$. These models are physically motivated in that they phenomenologically capture the behavior of thawing and freezing scalar field scenarios. While previous studies have primarily considered thawing quintessence as a non-crossing alternative, we find that a freezing phantom-like model is the only one capable of performing comparably to CPL--and only in a few cases. Nevertheless, across all dataset combinations considered, the standard CPL model consistently provides the best fit, strongly indicating that the data genuinely favor a PDL crossing.
papers.comments: 12 pages, 2 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D

papers.title: Constraints on Compact Dark Matter Population from Micro-lensing Effect of Gravitational Wave for the third-generation gravitational Wave Detector
papers.abstract: Since the first direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary black-hole merger by the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration, GWs have emerged as a powerful probe of astrophysics and cosmology. If extragalactic compact dark matter (DM) candidates, such as primordial black holes, constitute a non-negligible fraction of the DM component over a broad mass range, they can imprint distinctive microlensing signatures on GW signals. In this work, we develop a framework to infer the population properties of extragalactic compact DM by simulating microlensing GWs in the frequency band of the third-generation ground-based GW detector, the Einstein Telescope, and analyzing them via hierarchical Bayesian inference. For a population described by a power-law mass function, we show that the detection of only several microlensing GW events among $10^4$ binary black-hole coalescences can constrain the compact DMs abundance to the level of $\sim 10^{-3}$. This forecast demonstrates that searching for and identifying microlensing signatures in future GW observations can provide a complementary approach to constraining compact DM scenarios.
papers.comments: 10pages, 3 figures

papers.title: Eccentricity distribution of extreme mass ratio inspirals
papers.abstract: We present realistic eccentricity distributions for extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) forming via the two-body relaxation channel in nuclear star clusters, tracking their evolution up to the final plunge onto the central Schwarzschild massive black hole (MBH). We find that EMRIs can retain significant eccentricities at plunge, with a distribution peaking at $e_\mathrm{pl} \approx0.2$, and a considerable fraction reaching much higher values. In particular, up to $20\%$ of the forming EMRIs feature $e_\mathrm{pl} > 0.5$ for central MBH masses $M_\bullet$ in the range $10^5 \mathrm{M_\odot} \leq M_\bullet \leq 10^6 \mathrm{M_\odot}$, partially due to EMRIs forming at large semi-major axes and "cliffhanger EMRI", usually neglected in literature. This highlights the importance of accounting for eccentricity in waveform modeling and detection strategies for future space-based gravitational wave observatories such as the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). Furthermore, we find that the numerical fluxes in energy and angular momentum currently implemented in the FastEMRIWaveforms (FEW) package may not adequately sample the full parameter space relevant to low-mass MBHs ($M_\bullet < 10^6 \mathrm{M_\odot}$), potentially limiting its predictive power in that regime. Specifically, for $M_\bullet=10^5 \mathrm{M_\odot}$ we find that about $75\%$ ($50 \%$) of EMRIs at 2 years (6 months) from plunge fall outside the currently available flux parameter space. Our findings motivate the development of extended flux grids and improved interpolation schemes to enable accurate modeling of EMRIs across a broader range of system parameters.
papers.comments: 18 pages, 10 figures, 1 table; submitted to Phys. Rev. D; open data on Zenodo

papers.title: A two-phase model of galaxy formation: IV. Seeding and growing supermassive black holes in dark matter halos
papers.abstract: We present a theoretical framework for seeding and growing supermassive black holes (SMBHs) in dark matter halos along their assembly histories. Seeds are bred out of Pop-III stars formed during the first collapse of pristine gas in mini-halos that have reached the ${\rm H}_2$-cooling limit, modulated by UV radiation from star formation and dynamical heating from fast halo assembly. Such breeding persists until the enrichment of the intergalactic medium (IGM) enables Pop-II stars to form. Post-seeding growth of black holes (BHs) is driven by distinct channels, starting with episodic super-Eddington accretion associated with nuclear bursts induced by global disturbances of galaxies, followed by sustained sub-Eddington accretion via capturing sub-clouds formed in self-gravitating gas clouds (SGCs) in halos of fast assembly, and ending with merger-dominated, quiescent growth. We implement the model in subhalo merger trees to build a coherent framework to follow SMBH-galaxy-halo co-evolution across the whole history and structural hierarchy. BH seeds are bred with a broad mass spectrum of $M_{\rm BH} = 10$--$10^5\,{\rm M}_\odot$ at $z \approx 20$--$30$ in mini-halos with masses of $10^5$--$10^8\,{\rm M}_\odot$. Nuclear bursts provide the key condition for seeds to grow into SMBHs. The $M_{\rm BH}$-$M_*$ relation is a multi-piece, redshift-dependent function shaped by the interplay among different growth channels. Our model predictions are broadly consistent with existing observations; in particular, a population of BHs reminiscent of `little red dots' (LRDs) discovered by JWST naturally results from the seeding and growing processes. Potential future tests of the model are discussed.
papers.comments: 23 figures; 1 table. Accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Schwarzschild Spacetime and the Local Limit of Nonlocal Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate static spherically symmetric solutions within the framework of the local limit of nonlocal gravity. This theory departs from Einstein's general relativity (GR) through the introduction of a scalar gravitational susceptibility function $S(x)$, $1+S > 0$, which is a new feature of the spacetime that vanishes in the GR limit. It is shown that the Schwarzschild spacetime constitutes an exact solution of the modified source-free gravitational field equations provided $S$ is a constant. The mass of the corresponding Schwarzschild solution is given by $M/(1+S)$, where $M$ denotes the mass of the solution in the GR limit. The interpretation of the solution in terms of a black hole is ruled out due to the divergence of the algebraic invariants of the Weitzenböck torsion at the Schwarzschild horizon.
papers.comments: 26 pages; v2: presentation improved

papers.title: Possible photometric signatures of nebular-dominated emission in $1.5 < z < 8.5$ JADES galaxies
papers.abstract: The discovery of high-redshift galaxies exhibiting a steep spectral UV downturn potentially indicative of two-photon continuum emission marks a turning point in our search for signatures of top-heavy star formation in the early Universe. We develop a photometric search method for identifying further nebular-dominated galaxy candidates, whose nebular continuum dominates over the starlight, due to the high ionising photon production efficiencies $\xi_\mathrm{ion}$ associated with massive star formation. We utilise the extensive medium-band imaging from JADES, which enables the identification of Balmer jumps across a wide range of redshifts ($1.5 < z < 8.5$), through the deficit in rest-frame optical continuum level. As Balmer jumps are a general recombination feature of young starbursts ($\lesssim 3$ Myr), we further demand a high observed $\log\, (\xi_\mathrm{ion, obs}/\mathrm{(Hz\ erg^{-1})}) > 25.60$ to power the strong nebular continuum, together with a relatively non-blue UV slope indicating a lack of stellar continuum emission. Our nebular-dominated candidates, constituting ${\sim}$11% of galaxies at $z \sim 6$ (decreasing to ${\sim}$2% at $z \sim 2$, not completeness-corrected) are faint in the rest-frame optical (median $M_\mathrm{opt} = -17.95$) with extreme line emission (median $\mathrm{EW}_\mathrm{H\alpha,rest} = 1567$ Å, $\mathrm{EW}_\mathrm{[O\ III] + H\beta,rest} = 2292$ Å). However, hot H II region temperatures, collisionally-enhanced two-photon continuum emission, and strong UV lines are expected to accompany top-heavy star formation. Thus nebular-dominated galaxies do not necessarily exhibit the biggest Balmer jumps, nor the largest $\xi_\mathrm{ion, obs}$ or reddest UV slopes. Hence continuum spectroscopy is ultimately required to establish the presence of a two-photon downturn in our candidates, thus advancing our understanding of primordial star formation and AGN.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 27 pages, 17 figures, 1 table

papers.title: Magnetically supramassive and hypermassive compact stars
papers.abstract: It is known that the mass of a magnetized relativistic compact star is larger than that of non-magnetized one for the same equation of state and central density, albeit the excess of mass is sizable only if the magnetic fields are strong enough, B~10^17-10^18G. Using our recently developed numerical code COCAL, we systematically compute such compact star solutions in equilibrium associated with mixed poloidal and toroidal magnetic fields, and show the magnetically supramassive solutions whose masses exceed by more than 10% the maximum mass of the static and spherically symmetric solutions. For some extremely strong magnetic field configurations, we also obtain solutions more massive than the maximum mass of the uniformly rotating solutions at the Kepler (mass-shedding) limit, namely magnetically hypermassive solutions.
papers.comments: 14 pages

papers.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
papers.abstract: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 18 figures, 2 tables, Revised Version

papers.title: Nonconservative Lie series: post-Newtonian binary dynamics at 2.5PN
papers.abstract: We develop a Lie series perturbation method for solving the dynamics of nonconservative systems within the doubled phase-space Hamiltonian framework introduced in our previous work [PRE 113, 034137]. The procedure can be applied to a wide range of perturbed nonconservative systems which are not initially given by a Hamiltonian, by casting them into the doubled phase-space where the Lie method can be employed. As an application, we tackle the non-spinning $2.5$ post-Newtonian binary problem at leading dissipative order. Starting from the ADM radiation-reaction dynamics, we construct a resonant Birkhoff normal-form and the corresponding generator of the canonical transformation. Next, we establish an analytical perturbative solution accounting for both the long-term (secular) and short-term (oscillatory) temporal behavior, without performing a small-eccentricity expansion, for nondegenerate bound eccentric orbits. The secular piece is encoded in a resonant normal-form, and captures the long-term inspiral, reconstructing exactly the known Peters-Mathews relations for semi-major axis and eccentricity. The oscillatory piece completes the dynamics by supplying instantaneous, non-averaged corrections to the orbital parameters. Combined, the two pieces give a controlled, fully canonical description of the dissipative dynamics.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 0 figures

papers.title: Clustering redshift distribution calibration of weak lensing surveys using the DESI-DR1 spectroscopic dataset
papers.abstract: We estimate the source redshift distribution of current weak lensing surveys by applying the clustering-based redshift calibration technique, using the galaxy redshift sample provided by the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 1 (DESI-DR1). We cross-correlate the Bright Galaxy Survey (BGS), Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) and Emission Line Galaxies (ELGs) from DESI, within the redshift range $0.1 < z < 1.6$, with overlapping tomographic source samples from the Dark Energy Survey (DES), Kilo-Degree Survey (KiDS), and Hyper Suprime-Cam (HSC) survey. Using realistic mock catalogues, we test the stability of the clustering redshift signal to fitting scale, reference-sample choice, and the evolution of source galaxy bias. We calibrate a source galaxy bias correction from simulations with conservative (factor-of-two inflated) priors to account for modelling uncertainties, and we explicitly model and marginalise over magnification contributions, which become non-negligible at $z \gtrsim 1$ due to the depth of the DESI ELG sample. We then compare the resulting bias-weighted redshift distributions to \rossi{previously calibrated redshift distributions from the literature, based on self-organising map (SOM) techniques}, finding agreement within uncertainties for all surveys and tomographic bins. Our results demonstrate that clustering redshifts enabled by DESI's unprecedented spectroscopic sample provides a robust, complementary, and independent constraint capable of reducing one of the dominant systematic uncertainties in weak lensing cosmology.
papers.comments: Published in the Open Journal of Astrophysics, 20 pages, 10 figures

papers.title: Baryogenesis and EDMs in the 2HDM with a Complex Singlet
papers.abstract: We perform the first joint analysis of baryogenesis from initial Higgs charges (also called Higgsogenesis) and electric dipole moments (EDMs) in a model with two Higgs doublets, a complex scalar, and a Majorana fermion. In our proposed scenario, baryogenesis happens in three steps: (1) The decay of the scalar produces an asymmetry between the two Higgs doublets which is partly transferred to fermions via Standard Model processes. (2) This asymmetry is converted into a $B-L$ charge via interactions mediated by the Majorana fermion. (3) The weak sphaleron processes partially convert the resulting $B-L$ charge into a $B$ asymmetry. We perform a numerical analysis of baryogenesis and the EDM contributions and find that, due to resonant enhancement, baryogenesis is possible with singlet masses as low as $10^5$ GeV. We also find that for some parameters, the model can give large contributions to the electron and neutron EDM while also producing baryogenesis. The present scenario offers a new perspective on interpreting observational bounds in terms of cosmology: Because it relies on out-of-equilibrium decays, the questions of baryogenesis and $CP$ violation in the Higgs sector may be linked with EDM signals without the additional assumption of a first order electroweak phase transition.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 4 figures, matches journal version

papers.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
papers.abstract: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35\sigma$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.
papers.comments: 41 pages, 11 figures, 1 table

papers.title: Transitioning late-time cosmology with the Hubble parameterization
papers.abstract: We investigate a late-time cosmological model for a homogeneous and isotropic space-time in the Rastall theory. We explore the observational constraints on the Hubble parameter by using the latest cosmological datasets such as cosmic microwave background radiation (Planck), baryon acoustic oscillations (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae (Union 3.0). As a result, we explicitly demonstrate that the specific redshift transition occurs, namely, there happens a phase shift in the evolution of the universe from the initial deceleration era to the current accelerating phase of the cosmological scenario. Furthermore, we show that with the latest dataset of DESI-BAO clubbed with CC, CMB, and Union 3.0, the current value of the Hubble parameter is estimated as $H_0 = 66.945 \pm 1.094$, which can be compatible with the available observations.
papers.comments: 32 pages, 17 figures
papers.journal_ref: International Journal of Geometric Methods in Modern Physics, (2027) 2750012 (32 pages)

papers.title: Sound waves in a backreaction-affected analogue spacetime: acoustic metric, mass, and correlations in Bose-Einstein condensates
papers.abstract: Analogue gravity treats sound as a field on an effective spacetime set by the background flow, but quantum fluctuations feed back on this background. Whether a condensate modified by such backreaction still defines a spacetime for the quantum field remains open. Using a number-conserving expansion of a Bose-Einstein condensate, we show that in the sound-wave and eikonal approximations the first-order phase fluctuation propagates on an acoustic metric of the backreaction-corrected condensate and acquires a spacetime-dependent mass that cannot be absorbed into the metric. For a finite, quasi-one-dimensional gas after an interaction quench, backreaction enhances the equal-point phase correlation by about $10\%$ in the bulk and up to $20\%$ near the walls while the depletion remains below $2\%$; the bulk enhancement survives finite imaging resolution.

papers.title: Modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the IKKT model
papers.abstract: The gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the IKKT or IIB matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the Yang-Mills-type matrix action with the induced Einstein-Hilbert action. This combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified Einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. In particular we find extra non-Ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.
papers.comments: 27+10 pages, 4 figures. V2: harmonic gauge condition derived, improved presentation

papers.title: Spinning compact object and chaos in galactic centres
papers.abstract: Galactic centres are extremely complex environments, consisting primarily of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) surrounded by asymmetric mass distributions such as nuclear star clusters (NSC) and molecular gas, which form disks or halos. Together these components exert a gravitational field which, combined with relativistic corrections from the spin of the SMBH, generates strongly nonlinear dynamics and chaotic orbits. We model this region using a multipolar expansion potential, in which the central compact object is represented by the Artemova-Björnsson-Novikov pseudo-Newtonian potential, which mimics the spin dependence of a Kerr-like BH. The surrounding halo is modelled as an axisymmetric, shell-like mass distribution expanded to dipole order to induce asymmetry. Previous works have mostly quantified the chaos caused by the BH spin and dipole moment using Poincaré sections, SALI and other chaos indicators. In this study, we incorporate stability analysis and Newton-Raphson basins of convergence to provide a global view of the dynamics of the system. Stability analysis around fixed points gives deeper insight into the local behaviour, while basins of convergence show sensitivity to initial conditions and reveal fractal boundaries. Our results show that the BH spin substantially reshapes the equilibrium landscape. Depending on its magnitude, it can either intensify the chaos induced by the halo asymmetry or simplify the phase space. These results improve our understanding of how relativistic spin effects and multipole moments collectively affect particle motion in galactic centres.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 3 figures. Published in EPJ Web of Conferences (IEMPHYS-26 proceedings)

papers.title: Detection of Gravitational Anomaly at Low Acceleration from a Highest-quality Sample of 36 Wide Binaries with Accurate 3D Velocities
papers.abstract: We set out to accurately measure gravity in the low-acceleration range $(10^{-11},10^{-9})\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ from 3D motions of isolated wide binary stars. Gaia DR3 provides precise measurements of the four sky-plane components of the 3D relative displacement and velocity ($\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}$) for a system, but not comparably precise line-of-sight (radial) separation and velocity $v_{r}$. Based on our new observations and the public databases/publications, we assemble a sample of 36 nearby (distance $<150$pc) wide binaries in the low-acceleration regime with relatively accurate values of $v_r$. Kinematic contaminants such as undetected stellar companions are well under control using various observational diagnostics such as Gaia's {\tt ruwe} parameter, the color-magnitude diagram, multi-epoch observations of radial velocities, Speckle interferometric follow-up observations, and requiring Hipparcos-Gaia proper motion consistency. For $\Gamma \equiv \log_{10}\sqrt{\gamma}$ with $\gamma \equiv G/G_{\rm N}$ (where $G$ is a parameter generalizing Newton's constant $G_{\rm N}$), we find $\Gamma=0.102_{-0.021}^{+0.028}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ ($0.132_{-0.027}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$) giving a gravity boost factor of $\gamma=1.60_{-0.14}^{+0.24}$, which rules out Newton. This strong anomaly is dominated by two systems (the pairs of HD 189739, HD 189760, and TYC 259-236-1, TYC 259-906-1) that have 3D relative velocities exceeding their estimated Newtonian escape velocities. Without them, we have $\Gamma=0.042_{-0.024}^{+0.027}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, $0.057_{-0.031}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, and $0.085_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$ for $<10^{-10.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$. Future radial velocity monitoring and Speckle interferometric imaging for larger samples will be useful to refine the present result.
papers.comments: 41 pages (main part) + 39 pages (appendix), ApJ, revised (texts and references added on the Bayesian algorithm and independent solar-system results on gravity)

papers.title: Implications of a contracted dark matter halo for the Milky Way's inferred virial mass
papers.abstract: We investigate how reliably the global properties of Milky Way-mass dark matter haloes can be recovered from dynamical data from a limited range of radii, particularly $\lesssim 30~\mathrm{kpc}$ where observations are most sensitive but baryonic processes modify the halo structure. Using the ARTEMIS (Assembly of high-ResoluTion Eagle simulations of MIlkyWay-type galaxieS) simulations, which produce varying degrees of baryon-induced contraction, we fit dark matter profiles over restricted radial ranges using commonly adopted parametric models. Assuming negligible observational uncertainties allows the systematic errors from these choices to be isolated. When fits are confined to inner radii, a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) profile underestimates the virial mass by a factor of $\approx 2$ on average ($\approx 4$ for some systems), and the concentration by a factor of $\approx 2$. Einasto and generalized-NFW models provide excellent local fits but retain similar global biases. In contrast, a contracted halo prescription yields stable extrapolations and recovers unbiased halo mass estimates over all radii. The inferred mass improves systematically with increasing radial coverage, and tracers beyond $\gtrsim 50~\mathrm{kpc}$ largely eliminate the mean bias for all models. The local dark matter density at the Solar radius is recovered to within $\lesssim 5\%$ for all profiles other than NFW. These biases are sufficient to reconcile recent low Milky Way-mass estimates derived from inner rotation-curve analyses with the canonical $\approx 10^{12}~\mathrm{M}_\odot$. We additionally find a halo-to-halo scatter of $\gtrsim 0.1$ dex ($\approx 25\%$) persists even under idealized conditions, setting a likely lower limit for the precision of halo mass estimates.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Spectral Hierarchy of the Cosmic Web
papers.abstract: We introduce a spectral hierarchy of cosmic-web classifications obtained by applying simple scale-weighting kernels to the density field before performing a standard eigenvalue-based web classification. This unifies and extends several widely used web definitions within a single framework: the familiar potential/tidal web (large-scale, nonlocal), a curvature-based web (more local, peak- and ridge-sensitive), and additional higher-derivative levels that progressively emphasize smaller-scale structure. Because the classification is built from second derivatives of the filtered field, successive hierarchy levels align naturally with operator families that appear in renormalised bias and effective descriptions of large-scale structure, providing an explicit bridge between cosmic-web environments and long- and short-range nonlocal bias ingredients. We quantify the information content of the hierarchy with a compact statistic: we map each cell to one of four ordered web types (void, sheet, filament, knot), construct a corresponding ``web contrast'' field, and measure its cross-correlation with halos from the AbacusSummit simulation suite on a coarse mesh with $\Delta L\simeq 5.5\,h^{-1}\mathrm{Mpc}$. We find that the hierarchy retains significant tracer-relevant information from very large scales down to the mesh Nyquist limit, with the more local (curvature/higher-derivative) levels dominating toward nonlinear scales. This makes the spectral hierarchy a practical, interpretable conditioning basis for fast mock-galaxy production and field-level modelling, and a flexible tool for studying environment-dependent clustering and assembly bias.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 7 figures, 1 table, revised version

papers.title: Lensing in the Blue III: Weak Lensing Shape Catalogs of 30 Merging Galaxy Clusters
papers.abstract: We present the weak gravitational lensing dataset from the Super-pressure Balloon-Borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT), which imaged 30 galaxy clusters during its 45 night flight in April to May 2023. SuperBIT is a first-of-its-kind balloon-borne imaging telescope that achieved near diffraction-limited observations in near-space conditions above 98% of the Earth's atmosphere. We use the metacalibration algorithm to obtain calibrated galaxy shapes for our target clusters and several calibration fields, enabling unbiased reconstruction of the weak-lensing signal. We employ several diagnostics throughout the pipeline, including assessments of point-spread function (PSF) modeling residuals and their impact on weak-lensing measurements, as well as tests for correlations between galaxy shapes and measured galaxy and PSF properties. To assess the multiplicative shear bias of the pipeline, we analyze a parallel set of simulated images that incorporate the real observing conditions from the flight, including measured SuperBIT PSFs, observed sky backgrounds, and detector noise, yielding a bias of $(1.54 \pm 6.00)$ per cent.
papers.comments: 35 pages, 27 figures, 5 table; matches with the published version in ApJ

papers.title: Estimates of the Dynamic Characteristics of Binary Systems for Traversable Wormholes Search
papers.abstract: The paper presents simulated detectability of traversable wormholes (WHs) in wide binary astrophysical systems without accretion (dormant binary systems) and in the Galactic center. The wormhole spacetime is represented as a gluing of two asymptotically flat Schwarzschild spacetimes, without specifying the detailed geometry of the throat. The gravitational perturbation across the throat is calculated by matching the monopole perturbations on the two sides in the short-throat approximation. We consider a traversable WH candidate as a compact object in a binary system, whose companion star is perturbed by a massive object on an elliptical orbit on the other side of the WH throat. In the case of a supermassive BH as WH candidate the perturbing acceleration is analyzed and compared with the stochastic gravitational influence of surrounding stars. For dormant wide binary systems, we analyze the radial velocity perturbations and discuss how their signatures may differ from those of a triple system. We discuss the observational limits of our model arising due to the Keplerian orbit subtraction. Under the model assumptions and the considered observational sampling, radial velocity perturbations are detectable in simulations with an observational accuracy of 1.5 km/s for all considered observation time spans. For a more conservative accuracy of 5 km/s, the non-parametric analysis method becomes statistically significant after $\approx17$ years of simulated data accumulation. The spectral and non-parametric methods significantly reduce the required accumulation time compared to matched-filtering applied in isolation.
papers.comments: 38 pages, 10 figures

papers.title: GLIMPSED: Direct evidence for a fast active galactic nucleus-driven outflow from a z=6.64 little red dot host galaxy
papers.abstract: We report the discovery of GLIMPSED-329380, a z=6.64 galaxy behind Abell S1063, which shows signs of an extreme ionised outflow driven by an active galactic nucleus (AGN). The deep JWST/NIRSpec medium grating observations show spatially resolved structures of a host galaxy containing the very fast outflow and an AGN, which we analyse separately. The outflow, mainly traced by broad [O III]{\lambda}5008 and H{\alpha} emissions in the host, reaches a full-width-at-half-maximum velocity of ~5350km/s, velocities only observed in AGN-dominated systems. From the Balmer decrement, we observe that while the narrow emission lines show no dust attenuation, the outflowing gas is dusty. We use emission lines diagnostics to infer gas abundances within the host galaxy. The oxygen abundance is 12+log(O/H)~7.96 (~18% solar) and the host is slightly nitrogen-enriched with log(N/O) ~ -0.68. Unless the extreme outflow turns out to be very dusty, the mass loading factor (>5-10%), and the kinetic energy (>1e43erg/s) of the extreme outflow does not hint at a significant impact on the galaxy. The AGN component shows many similarities with little red dots (LRDs): a characteristic 'V shape', exponential profile in hydrogen lines, numerous detection of forbidden [Fe II] lines, a Balmer break, and a broad absorption feature at ~4550Å. This detection of a fast outflow in an LRD, rare in surveys dominated by low-resolution (e.g. PRISM) spectra, provides direct evidence of AGN activity in these systems.
papers.comments: 17 pages, Published in A&A

papers.title: Classical and quantum evolution of inflationary fluctuations
papers.abstract: We compare the correlation functions of inflationary perturbations computed either with quantum or classical dynamics. Even if they are enforced to agree at a specific time during inflation, classical and quantum correlations will differ at the end of inflation, provided that interactions are relevant. The difference between the results of the classical and quantum computations is exponentially sensi- tive to the number of e-folds elapsed from the time of agreement. We illustrate this finding with the tree-level bispectrum of the primordial curvature fluctuation and the one-loop power spectrum of tensor modes. We also show that classical evolution from a finite time does not imply the appearance of poles in the scalar bispectrum.
papers.comments: 5 pages plus 2 appendices. Introduction partially rewritten. Results unchanged

papers.title: Cosmological discrete self-similarity in primordial black hole formation
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that discrete self-similarity (DSS), originally discovered in the asymptotically flat collapse of a massless scalar field, survives in primordial black hole (PBH) formation within an expanding cosmological background. Using fully relativistic simulations of massless scalar-field collapse in a Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universe, we resolve the near-critical regime and find clear log-periodic oscillations in the PBH mass-scaling relation. This result provides a proof of principle that PBHs may retain information about the critical behaviour in their formation realized in the early Universe: PBH formation in scalar-field kination exhibits DSS, while radiation-fluid collapse is characterized by continuous self-similarity. The resulting mass scaling imprints characteristic log-periodic modulations in an illustrative PBH mass spectrum, which may survive when PBH formation is dominated by a sufficiently narrow range of scales, with possible consequences for PBH phenomenology. Our results show that PBHs may encode not only the amplitude of primordial perturbations, but also the nature of the matter sector and the dynamical state of the Universe at horizon re-entry.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 9 figures, including Supplemental Material. Published version in Physical Review D Letters

papers.title: Machine learning technique for morphological classification of galaxies from SDSS. IV. CNN-Assisted Expert Validation of Morphological Catalogues for Merging, Irregular, Edge-on, Barred, Ringed, and Dust-lane Galaxies at 0.003 < z < 0.1
papers.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) classify galaxy morphology efficiently in large surveys, but complex features remain affected by projection effects, image artefacts, and intrinsic ambiguities, so expert visual validation is essential for reliable catalogues. We apply a CNN-assisted expert validation framework to SDSS galaxies at 0.003 < z < 0.1 previously classified by a CNN as merging, irregular, edge-on, barred, ringed, and dust-lane systems. We visually inspected all CNN-selected candidates in four categories - merging (2574), irregular (9432), ringed (13882), and dust-lane (588) - over their full catalogue feature-score range; for edge-on and barred galaxies we inspected the 17000 and 4323 highest-scoring candidates from larger CNN catalogues. Galaxies outside the Galaxy Zoo 2 (GZ2) selection domain, which carry no GZ2 label, were classified here. For the subset with SDSS spectroscopy we applied the BPT and WHAN diagnostics to MPA-JHU emission-line measurements. The verified catalogues contain 612 merging, 9372 irregular, 16822 edge-on, 811 barred, 2145 ringed, and 575 dust-lane galaxies. Comparison with GZ2 shows that this validation both refines existing classifications and extends reliable catalogues beyond the effective Galaxy Zoo selection domain. CNN misclassification is driven mainly by projection effects, foreground stars, faint tidal structures, and intrinsically ambiguous morphologies. Emission-line diagnostics show that 87.8% of the ringed galaxies with LINER-like line ratios have H-alpha equivalent widths consistent with ionisation by evolved stars rather than by an active nucleus. We also identify five strong new candidates for polar-ring galaxies. The catalogues provide benchmark samples for studies of galaxy morphology, secular evolution and nuclear activity, and for future machine-learning applications.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 11 figures, 3 tables, 84 references, accepted to A&A

papers.title: Metastability Landscapes in Nonlinear Ghost-Normal Scalar Fields
papers.abstract: We investigate finite time dynamics in nonlinear classical scalar field systems containing one ghost and one normal kinetic sector. Using a spacetime finite element formulation, we study the dependence of threshold crossing and numerical continuation times on initial amplitude, characteristic wavenumber, spectral tilt, phase structure, and spatial localization. In the quartic model, larger amplitudes generally lead to earlier growth, while higher wavenumbers and ultraviolet-biased spectra favor longer resolved bounded evolution. Smooth compact initial data exhibit a broad region with no observed growth threshold crossing over the simulated interval. A direct comparison of two Gaussian evolutions shows that enhanced low-wavenumber power can precede rapid field growth, although this observation does not establish a universal spectral-transfer mechanism. We also compare the quartic interaction with a lifted $\phi^6$ potential. The latter gives a markedly different continuation landscape, with a broad long-converged region followed by shorter accessible terminal times at larger amplitudes. Localization diagnostics do not identify a persistent oscillon core in the selected cases. By distinguishing amplitude growth, spectral reorganization, solver-limited termination, and finite-time censoring, our results characterize a nontrivial metastability landscape without implying global or quantum stability.
papers.comments: 28 pages (including 14 figures and 6 tables) with 3 appendices and references

papers.title: Vision-Language Model Ensembles Achieve Human-Expert Accuracy for Galaxy Merger Classification
papers.abstract: Models (VLMs) combined using a Bayesian statistical framework can classify galaxy merger morphologies with accuracy comparable to trained human experts. We deploy 15 VLM classifier configurations, spanning four model architectures (Gemma-4 E2B, Gemma-4 E4B, Qwen2.5-VL, and Qwen3-VL) tested with up to four prompt engineering strategies each. We evaluate their performance against a truth-known sample of 41 VELA+SUNRISE mock galaxy images from Lambrides et al. (2021a). As a proof-of-concept, all validation is performed on these mock images; application to real observational samples will require additional calibration and observational validation. The VLM ensemble achieves 83.3% accuracy on confident classifications (merger probability pM >= 0.8 or pM <= 0.2) and 58.3% completeness, with 5 misclassified galaxies, compared to 85% for both human accuracy and completeness. The ensemble recovers the population merger fraction to within 0.66 sigma of the truth (fM = 0.52 +/- 0.09 vs. true value of 0.585). Bayesian weighting improves overall accuracy by 17.1 percentage points over simple majority voting, with sensitivity improving by 29.2 percentage points. The ensemble produces 5 misclassifications (2 false positives, 3 false negatives), comparable to the 6 misclassifications (5 false positives, 1 false negative) reported for human classifiers by L21. The error-profile differences are not statistically significant for this sample. VLMs also produce more moderate per-galaxy merger probability distributions (27% uncertain) than the more polarized human distributions (15% uncertain), though this difference is also consistent with statistical fluctuation. These results establish VLMs as scalable, reproducible alternatives to human classifiers within a Bayesian probabilistic merger-fraction framework, for large-survey applications.
papers.comments: This work used LLMs as research assistants for code development, statistical analysis, and drafting under close human supervision; the workflow is described in Appendix A. Accepted for publication in the Astronomical Journal

papers.title: Effect of $ξRϕ^2$ non-minimal coupling on gravitational light bending
papers.abstract: We investigate the bending of massless fields by a massive object in the presence of a curvature-scalar $\sqrt{-g}\xi R \phi^2$ non-minimal coupling up to one loop, using the perturbative quantum gravity computations. It is well known that without such coupling a self interacting scalar field theory cannot be renormalised in the presence of gravity. The massive object is modelled by a massive scalar $\phi$, and it is assumed to be non-relativistic, e.g., a star. We compute the 2-2 scattering of massless scalar and photons off this object via graviton exchanges. Assuming both $\xi$ and the bending angle to be small, we use the eikonal approximation to compute the angle up to ${\cal O}(\xi G^2)$. At tree level $({\cal O}(\xi G))$ we find no bending, and hence the ${\cal O}(\xi G^2)$ result happens to be leading in this case. The non-minimal vertices are qualitatively different from that of the standard minimal ones, e.g. $ \sqrt{G} h_{\mu\nu} T^{\mu\nu}$, as the former contains explicit momenta of the gravitons instead of the scalar, complementing the second. The bending angle is found to behave like $\sim b^{-7}$, where $b$ is the impact parameter. We have emphasised the qualitative differences of our results from that of the well studied minimal case.
papers.comments: v2; 14pp, 3 figs; revised version, introduction and discussion updated, references added, accepted in PLB

papers.title: A Census of the 200 Most Massive Galaxies Spectroscopically Observed with JWST at zspec $\sim$3-15
papers.abstract: Massive galaxies provide strong tests of galaxy formation models, yet a comprehensive spectroscopic view of their properties and demographics in the early Universe has remained elusive. Here we present a JWST spectroscopic census of the 200 most massive galaxies at zspec~3-15, selected using an evolving stellar-mass threshold motivated by the halo mass function and anchored at log(Mstar)>10 at z~5. These galaxies represent the top 3% most massive systems among all publicly available prism observations. We derive their physical properties through joint SED fitting of spectroscopy and photometry, and construct a clean massive galaxy sample after removing LRDs and broad-line AGN contaminants. We find that the massive galaxy population evolves strongly with redshift: normal SFGs (Av<1 mag) dominate at z>~6, while dusty SFGs (Av>1 mag) and QGs become more common toward lower redshift. Dust attenuation decreases systematically toward higher redshift. We identify 29 massive QGs, including a population of recently quenched systems whose star formation declined rapidly within the past ~100 Myr. We further show that both the traditional UVJ and recently proposed (ugi)s selections suffer substantial inconsistency with the most massive galaxies at z>3, motivating a revised (ugi)s criterion calibrated using our spectroscopic sample. The inferred formation histories suggest at least two pathways toward quiescence: a dust-enriched pathway linking normal SFGs, dusty SFGs, and QGs, and a more direct pathway connecting normal SFGs and QGs. Massive normal SFGs appear to grow through both relatively gradual and rapid assembly modes. Together, these results suggest that rapid stellar-mass assembly, dust enrichment, and quenching were already shaping the evolutionary pathways of the most massive galaxies within the first billion years after the Big Bang.
papers.comments: 23 pages (16 main text, 7 appendix), 16 figures, 9 tables. Resubmitted to A&A after revision. The massive galaxies catalog is available at this https URL

papers.title: Dissipative hydrodynamic actions and horizon symmetries in gravity
papers.abstract: We give a prescription to compute a dissipative action describing the large-scale thermal stress tensor dynamics of a holographic quantum field theory dual to AdS$_4$ gravity, in the context of the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism. Our prescription is valid to quadratic order in perturbations about the thermal equilibrium state. The hydrodynamical degrees of freedom of this action are realised in gravity as relative diffeomorphisms between the black hole horizon and the two asymptotic boundaries of the Crossley-Glorioso-Liu contour. We explicitly compute the action to first order in derivatives, and confirm it correctly reproduces the known hydrodynamic Green's functions. Our prescription requires a choice of horizon boundary conditions for the metric. We study the horizon symmetries that preserve these, and their relation to conjectured hydrodynamic symmetries responsible for many-body quantum chaos.
papers.comments: 56 pages (including refs), 1 figure. v2: improved presentation slightly, added Weyl-invariant form of the hydro action, updated refs, main results unchanged, accepted in JHEP

papers.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
papers.abstract: We present the results of a deep 251 ks XRISM/Resolve observation of the cool core of the galaxy cluster Abell 2199. From the integrated spectrum of the central $3' \times 3'$ Resolve field of view ($104 \times 104 \mathrm{~kpc}^2$), we find that the intracluster medium (ICM) redshift is consistent with that of the brightest cluster galaxy, within the optical-redshift uncertainty. This indicates that they form a kinematically coherent core system, which is offset from the mean cluster redshift by $\sim200~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. The observed velocity dispersion of $\sim100~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ corresponds to a three-dimensional Mach number of $M_{\mathrm{3D}}=0.16$ and a non-thermal pressure fraction of $P_{\mathrm{NT}}/P_{\mathrm{tot}}=1.4\pm0.2$%. Abell 2199 is one of the most dynamically quiescent relaxed clusters observed with XRISM, despite the presence of radio jets and a plume-like structure possibly associated with sloshing motions. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that turbulent dissipation could offset a non-negligible fraction of the radiative cooling losses, with $Q_{\mathrm{turb}}/Q_{\mathrm{cool}}\approx0.2$ for a large-scale driver such as sloshing and larger values for smaller AGN-feedback scales. Finally, we detect a localized enhancement of the Fe XXV He$\alpha$ $y$ line in the southeast region, which spatially coincides with a Chandra surface brightness discontinuity.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, Submitted to PASJ

papers.title: Leptogenesis with sub-electroweak-scale reheating temperature
papers.abstract: We study the generation of the baryon asymmetry of the Universe via leptogenesis during the post-inflationary reheating epoch, considering reheating temperatures below the temperature of sphaleron freeze-out. Within the framework of a monomial inflaton potential during reheating, we analyze three perturbative reheating scenarios in which the inflaton decays into (i) a pair of Standard Model (SM)-like bosons, (ii) a pair of SM-like fermions, or (iii) exclusively into a pair of heavy right-handed neutrinos, which eventually decays into the SM final states after briefly dominating the energy density of the Universe. For each case, we identify the regions of parameter space that successfully reproduce the observed baryon asymmetry consistently tracking the sphaleron interaction rate during reheating, while satisfying existing cosmological constraints. We also highlight the potential of future primordial gravitational wave observations to probe this class of scenarios.
papers.comments: 43 pages, 20 captioned figures, improved calculations, figures updated, matches the version accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D

papers.title: Probing the matter-dominated expansion with multi-redshift Lyman-$α$ BAO from DESI DR2
papers.abstract: We present a multi-redshift Baryon Acoustic Oscillations (BAO) analysis of the DESI Data Release 2 (DR2) Lyman-$\alpha$ (Ly$\alpha$) forest, splitting the forest auto-correlation and its cross-correlation with quasars into three redshift bins. We obtain BAO measurements at effective redshifts $z_{\rm eff} = 2.13$, $2.40$, and $2.81$ with $\sim2.0$--$2.5\%$ precision per bin in the radial and transverse directions, corresponding to $\sim1.1$--$1.2\%$ precision for the isotropic BAO measurement. Using the same data products and modeling framework as the DESI DR2 Ly$\alpha$ BAO analysis, we validate the pipeline on $400$ synthetic datasets and find unbiased BAO recovery with well-calibrated uncertainties.
